chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, who said: He told me, Muhammad ibn Ahmad, saying: He told me, Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from Sajjada, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

There is no feast (walimah) except in five occasions: marriage, circumcision, buying a house, or a man's return from Mecca. As for the 'urs, it is marriage; and the 'idhar is circumcision; and the wikar is the one who buys a house; and the rikaz is when a man arrives from Mecca.
ai.seo_question: What are the five occasions for holding a walimah feast according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to delineate the five specific occasions for hosting a walimah, emphasizing the Prophet's guidance on social joy and community bonding. Notably, the inclusion of 'returning from Mecca' (rikaz) highlights the spiritual significance of the Hajj pilgrimage in Shia jurisprudence, while 'purchasing a home' (wikar) underscores the importance of domestic stability. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the permissibility and recommended timing of celebratory feasts in Islamic social life.
